findings.title: Possible broken object level authorization (BOLA)
findings.description: An authenticated endpoint takes an object ID from the path and returns or changes that object. No 403 was ever observed, so there is no sign that ownership is checked.
findings.detail: GET /customers/{customerId} (customer-self-service-backend): object ID from path, response carries owner field customerId, 0 x 403 in 40 calls
factors: likelihood -1: reachable only inside the cluster
findings.recommendation: Add an ownership check to GET /customers/{customerId} in customer-self-service-backend.
mitigation: Check that the object belongs to the caller (or that the caller's role allows it) on every access.
Return 404 for objects the caller does not own, so IDs cannot be enumerated.
Prefer random IDs (UUIDs) over sequential integers.

findings.title: Login has no visible brute-force protection
findings.description: The login endpoint returned failures but never a 429 or lockout, and no rate-limiting directive in the gateway or Ingress configuration covers it, so password guessing is not being slowed down.
findings.detail: POST /auth (customer-self-service-backend): 15 failed logins, no 429 seen
factors: likelihood -1: reachable only inside the cluster
evidence: no rate-limiting directive on its gateway route or Ingress
findings.recommendation: Add rate limiting and lockout to /auth.
mitigation: Rate-limit login per account and per IP (e.g. 5 failures / 15 min) and return 429.
Add MFA for privileged accounts and alert on failure spikes.

findings.title: No network segmentation for the service
findings.description: No NetworkPolicy selects this workload, so every pod in the cluster can call it. One compromised pod can move laterally.
findings.detail: customer-core accepts traffic from any pod

mitigation: Add a default-deny NetworkPolicy for the namespace, then allow only the callers seen in traces.
